title: AI agents hack at scale, but the novel exploit leap still came from a human
description:
AI agents hunt at scale, and the novel exploit chain still required a human to invent. At Black Hat, security researcher James Kettle worked with AI to uncover Shared Parser Confusion, a new vulnerability class where two parts of a system read the same input differently. The models accelerated his pursuit at formidable speed. The conceptual leap connecting those pieces into a novel chain came from Kettle himself. That boundary gives defenders something concrete to build around: a specific, evidence-based picture of where autonomous capability actually sits. As the line between human-led and autonomous offensive capability continues to shift, knowing its current position turns security strategy from guesswork into engineering.
